candidate_sentences.text: Eleving Group reported strong financial growth during the 2024 reporting year, achieving record levels across key metrics.
Revenue increased by 15% to EUR 216.6 million, driven by robust loan issuance volumes that grew 26.8% year-over-year to EUR 368.6 million.

The net loan portfolio expanded by 16% to reach EUR 371.2 million, supported by successful integration of acquired Sub-Saharan operations and sustained demand across European and East African markets.
Total net profit reached an all-time high of EUR 29.6 million, representing a 21% increase compared to 2023.

Operating performance was further strengthened by a record EBITDA of EUR 89.8 million, up more than 16% from the prior year, while impairment expenses remained relatively stable despite portfolio expansion, aided by disciplined underwriting and improved non-performing loan ratios.

verified_key_information_units.information: Key year-over-year improvements included a 29.3% capitalization ratio (vs 26.1% in 2023), 2.4 interest coverage ratio (vs 2.3), and reduced net leverage to 3.3x (from 3.7x).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management report financial highlights; Note 48 Alternative Performance Measures

candidate_sentences.text: The capitalization ratio rose to 29.3%, and net leverage decreased to 3.3 times, enhancing financial flexibility.

verified_key_information_units.information: Major performance drivers were organic growth in Europe/Africa, successful integration of Sub-Saharan operations (tripling regional portfolio), digital transformation (doubled applications, new self-service platform), and enhanced risk management improving portfolio quality.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: CEO keynote; Management report operations section

candidate_sentences.text: The net loan portfolio expanded by 16% to reach EUR 371.2 million, supported by successful integration of acquired Sub-Saharan operations and sustained demand across European and East African markets.
Operationally, the Group completed the rollout of its next-generation digital self-service platform across Europe, nearly doubling customer applications and strengthening operational efficiency.

Concurrently, the subsidiary in Sub-Saharan Africa accelerated sustainable mobility initiatives, financing nearly 2,000 electric motorcycles and meeting long-term environmental targets ahead of schedule.

verified_key_information_units.information: Business segments showed vehicle finance (67% of portfolio: 45% traditional, 20% flexible/subscription) and consumer finance (33%: Kredo, Tigo, etc.), with key growth in East Africa (e-motorcycles), Romania, Uganda, and Albania offsetting exits from Balkan/Belarus.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management report segments; Sustainability statement portfolio balance; Note 19 discontinued operations

candidate_sentences.text: The net loan portfolio expanded by 16% to reach EUR 371.2 million, supported by successful integration of acquired Sub-Saharan operations and sustained demand across European and East African markets.

The Group also finalized exits from non-core markets in Belarus and the Balkans, with discontinued operations generating a profit of EUR 0.8 million.

verified_key_information_units.information: Capital structure transformed via October 2024 IPO raising EUR 29.0 mln equity (largest in Nasdaq Riga history), used to repay subordinated bonds and high-cost Mintos loans, while expanding local currency funding (Kenya +30%, Botswana notes).

candidate_sentences.text: The period was defined by several strategic milestones, most notably the company’s successful initial public offering in October, which raised EUR 29.0 million in equity through the largest listing in Nasdaq Riga’s history.
The capital raised was promptly deployed to redeem expensive subordinated borrowings and reduce funding costs, resulting in a significantly improved balance sheet.

verified_key_information_units.information: Strategic priorities include deepening existing markets, broadening product portfolio (e.g., electric motorcycle financing surpassing 2025 targets), geographic expansion, and developing ESG strategy for 2026-2031 with climate neutrality targets for HQ operations.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Business outlook; Sustainability framework; CEO keynote

candidate_sentences.text: Operationally, the Group completed the rollout of its next-generation digital self-service platform across Europe, nearly doubling customer applications and strengthening operational efficiency.

Concurrently, the subsidiary in Sub-Saharan Africa accelerated sustainable mobility initiatives, financing nearly 2,000 electric motorcycles and meeting long-term environmental targets ahead of schedule.

Overall, the company delivered resilient top-line and bottom-line expansion, optimized its capital structure, and advanced its digital and sustainability strategies while maintaining strict credit discipline.

The narrative flows from overall performance highlights (S1) through revenue and profit details (S2-S5), operational milestones (S6-S7), capital structure improvements (S8-S9), and strategic initiatives (S10-S13). Explanations are consistent (e.g., S5 clarifies the adjusted net profit), comparisons are logical (e.g., S2-S4 show growth metrics), and the summary forms a clear, non-repetitive whole.
